An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf retr 30
div.ab: De hundredis et wapentagiis, et quare wapentac uocatur. (Quid sit wapentagium, et qualiter se agebant qui wapentagium accipiebant.) Euerwichescire, Nicolescire, Notingehamscire, Leircestrescire, Norhamtunescire, usque ad Watlingestret et VIII (miliaria) ultra Watlingastret sub lege Anglorum.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 652 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.
Liebermann’s footnote e (Anglorum for Danorum) is printed under the ECf column; it is given here in part.

note.seg: bessere Danorum: Verf. meint Denalagu.

div.ab: Concerning hundreds and wapentakes, and why it is called wapentake. (What a wapentake is, and how those who received a wapentake conducted themselves.) Yorkshire, Lincolnshire, Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire, Northamptonshire, as far as Watling Street and eight (miles) beyond Watling Street, under the law of the English.
